pr_body:
Cluster state role mappings need to be recovered from disk CS
(when master nodes are restarted), because the CS metadata
that says if the role mappings are up to date (it actually tells
if all file settings are up to date) is itself recovered from disk.
In case that the metadata is recovered, but the role mappings
themselves are not, the role mappings from the file will not
be present in the CS and will also not be copied from the
settings file.

Fixes: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/93048
pr_title: Fixes cluster state-based role mappings not recovered from disk

review_comment: This is the IT that exercises that role mappings are recovered from disk CS.
This is the essential part of this PR.
changes in this file are just to expose some methods to reuse in another test

This further tightly couples the payload of our REST API to the payload of cluster state, despite the workflow being disjoint. I think this is fine for now, but it does present some long term concern w.r.t. these objects and the tight coupling of their serialization. The mismatch between persisted state across multiple versions of ES vs. transient state in a REST API yields different expectations and want to protect against good nature changes in the REST API breaking cluster state and vice-versa. Given the impact of getting this wrong at some future point, can you follow up with something that decouples these two ? Perhaps an adaptor pattern, where today it is an identity adaption (e.g. no differences) but is explicit and tests that changes to one will not influence the other. (or just duplicate the code between them)
You're right to point out that this is an issue. I'll follow-up with an implementation of "`ExpressionRoleMapping` in the CS" separate from "`ExpressionRoleMapping` in request payload".
